items.q: What two questions does Jeong treat as a kill-switch before you found?
items.a: **Why this company, and why you.** Nobody assigned the job. When it is lonely, only you can answer. If you face yourself and the answer is unclear: **do not start.**

items.q: How does a mission-driven founder label the same stretch outsiders call a hard time?
items.a: **Building time.** They say risk; you say opportunity. Without a true mission the reframe is cosplay — quit.

items.q: What PMF culture did Noom build after the untested bike?
items.a: **Test → learn → humble.** Being in love with the product is the wrong signal. They do not wait for one genius to prove it. Most ideas fail. When fit arrives they call that **luck**, then scale.

items.q: What is the upside of the immigrant seat, per Jeong?
items.a: Nothing you think is normal is automatically normal. That cost is also a **sensor**: you see broken service locals walk past. Fortunate **and** difficult.

items.q: What common habit has Jeong seen in billionaires, and what is his ritual?
items.a: **Discipline + long-term resource allocation**, not a hunt for the quick return. His: early wake, exercise, daily meditation, breaks between meetings. Drink to **celebrate**, not to manage stress.

items.q: What does he tell teens, 20s, and 30s?
items.a: **Teens:** don't prove yourself on a feed; ask seniors what talent they see; students are forgiven for errors. **20s:** school taught you how to study; stay **6–12 months** in one path. **30s:** keep disrupting or the same decade repeats through 40s and 50s.
